title: From Context to Memory: Your Agents Need a Real Memory Layer — Anders Swanson, Oracle
talk_summary: The talk argues that context windows and file scratchpads are not durable memory; agents need a governed memory layer that forms distilled typed memories, retrieves them with hybrid search, and evolves them via feedback and lifecycle controls. It outlines mechanisms for redaction, scoping, provenance, conflict/stale handling, and measurable recall, mostly framed around Oracle's multi-model database.

takeaways.what_they_do: They persist distilled facts, procedures, episodes, and working state with metadata instead of raw transcripts, then reconstruct context per run from retrieved memories.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Context windows are are not memory. Um they're the input for the current run and not a persistent experience.
hybrid retrieval is emerging as a dominant method. This is This is a form of retrieval that fuses different types of search.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before embedding or enriching a memory, they redact secrets/PII, then add scope metadata, embeddings, and provenance links to the source episode.
takeaways.evidence_quote: redaction is very important as the first step because before I do embeddings, before I do enrichment, I want to strip out PII.

takeaways.what_they_do: They scope memories by agent, workflow, team, and organization on write and read so unrelated sessions do not pollute each other's context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This helps bucket into specific areas so I'm not getting memories in other sessions that are associated with other agents or workflows

takeaways.what_they_do: They record whether retrieved memories were used, rejected, helpful, stale, or harmful, and feed that back into ranking and lifecycle decisions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if if the memory was harmful, the feedback should go down. If it was useful, maybe we promote it.

takeaways.what_they_do: They track validity, last use, duplicates, and conflicts, and require review/suppression when memories become stale or contradictory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: stale memory can occur when, say, my my project uses NPM at one time and then we decide to switch to another build system.
